stem: Widderburn Analytics re-runs `terraform apply` on a configuration that already created a specific database instance. Nothing about that resource's configuration changed, yet Terraform still needs to know it already exists so it does not try to create a duplicate. What provides that link?

choices.text: The state file's mapping, which records the identity of the already-created object against that particular resource block.
The block that declares the provider and its version constraint, which lists which provider owns the database resource type.
The resource block's own arguments; identical settings will always resolve to the same real object.
The file that records installed provider versions and checksums, which tracks every resource ever created by a given provider version.

rationale: State's mapping purpose records the identity of the already-created remote object against that specific resource block, which is exactly the link needed to avoid a duplicate. `required_providers` only names which provider and version are needed, unrelated to tracking a specific created object. Identical arguments do not by themselves identify one particular already-created object; without a recorded mapping, re-running could create a second object with the same settings. The dependency lock file tracks provider versions and checksums, not individual created resources.
